_comment: CED-tiny (mispeech/ced-tiny rev ace276d2) front-end, read from source NOT memory. Sources: models/ced-tiny/feature_extraction_ced.py (CedFeatureExtractor), preprocessor_config.json, config.json, and runtime introspection of torchaudio 2.4.1 MelSpectrogram/AmplitudeToDB. This is the standard the collar C log-mel must match.
input: float32 mono PCM in [-1,1] (collar int16 / 32768.0). Model inference unit = a W-second window (presence 1.0s, type 2.0s), cropped with zero-pad past edges (serve/embed.py::crop) BEFORE the front-end.

mel_spectrogram.impl: torchaudio.transforms.MelSpectrogram (defaults not overridden are pinned below by introspection)
mel_spectrogram.window: hann, periodic=True (torch.hann_window(512, periodic=True); sum=256.0; NOT symmetric)
mel_spectrogram.mel_fb_note: filterbank [257,64], NOT slaney-normalized (per-filter column sum ~=3.9, not 1.0). fb computed by torchaudio.functional.melscale_fbanks(htk, norm=None).

amplitude_to_db.formula_clamp: x_db = max(x_db, x_db.max() - 120.0)   <-- x_db.max() is over the WHOLE W-second window

operations_after_log_before_patch_embed.note: model is in .eval() -> uses FIXED running_mean/running_var buffers, NOT per-segment stats. Per-frame safe. Ship the running stats to C or keep server-side.
deterministic given T; a 1s/2s window (T<=~201 frames) is < 1012 so n_splits=1, no split.

operations_after_log_before_patch_embed.step: flatten+permute, transformer blocks x12, final norm

encoder_boundary.front_end_output: log-mel [B, 64, T] after AmplitudeToDB (feature_extraction_ced.py::__call__ returns BatchFeature input_values)
encoder_boundary.encoder_entry: modeling_ced.py CedModel.forward, line 421 (x = torch.unsqueeze(input_values, 1)). init_bn + patch_embed are inside the encoder.

whole_segment_dependent.why: clamp min = x_db.max() - 120, max taken over the entire W-second window (in serve/embed.py the feature extractor is called per inference window, so max is per-window, NOT per whole session).
whole_segment_dependent.handling: collar uploads PRE-top_db log-mel = 10*log10(max(mel_power,1e-10)) per frame; server reconstructs the W-second window (it already does the windowing) and applies the top_db window clamp inside encode_from_logmel before the encoder. (Alternatively verify top_db is inactive for the signal range and drop it — to be decided in Step 1/2, not assumed here.)

whole_segment_dependent.op: center=True reflect padding at WINDOW edges
whole_segment_dependent.why: The current waveform path runs the front-end on each W-second window INDEPENDENTLY (serve/embed.py::crop then fe per window). With center=True the STFT reflect-pads n_fft//2=256 samples at each window edge, so the first ~2 and last ~2 frames of every window are built from MIRRORED audio. A continuous per-frame collar computes those same frame positions from REAL neighbouring audio -> the edge frames differ between the two paths.
whole_segment_dependent.handling: ref_logmel.py STREAM mode frames the WHOLE recording continuously (frame k centered at sample k*160), reflect-padding only at the recording's absolute start/end; the server then slices by frame index into the same W-second encoding windows. So the collar never reflect-pads at window boundaries; only the single recording-start boundary is padded (padding rule is an explicit ref_logmel parameter). Interior window edges therefore use real audio, unlike the HF per-window path. Step 2 must quantify the edge-frame delta (first/last ~2 frames) and its effect on the embedding.
whole_segment_dependent.frame_radius_affected: n_fft//2 / hop_length = 256/160 ~= 1.6 -> first/last 2 frames per window

pcm_scaling.mono: multi-channel averaged to mono before scaling
pcm_scaling.resample: if sr != 16000, scipy.signal.resample_poly to 16k (collar is native 16k, so no resample on device)

pre_frontend_processing.pre_emphasis: NONE (no pre-emphasis filter anywhere in embed.py or feature_extraction_ced.py)
pre_frontend_processing.dc_removal: NONE (no DC/mean subtraction before the STFT)
pre_frontend_processing.note: the only thing before MelSpectrogram is int16/32768 scaling + mono + (optional) resample. Confirmed by reading serve/embed.py and feature_extraction_ced.py.

must_be_server_side: init_bn + split/pad + patch_embed + transformer (the encoder itself)
placement_conclusion.note: init_bn in eval mode is per-frame safe (fixed buffers) but lives inside the encoder, so it stays server-side anyway. The ONLY front-end op the collar cannot do per-frame is the top_db window clamp.
